mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for three consecutive months, combined with a rising unemployment rate, indicates labor market imbalances that can precede a recession and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases sensitivity to income shocks and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).
